name: Dual-Sector Kinetic-Orthogonal Stiff-Vector (DSKOSV)
claimed_mechanism: The MOND force law is derived from the constraint algebra C_M = D_i[\mu(y)D^i q] - 4\pi G \rho \approx 0 (auxiliary Legendre \chi). The preferred-frame sector is a 3-DOF stiff vector u_mu whose kinetic structure is strictly orthogonal to the MOND constraint. The e^-y screening factor multiplies the PPN-visible preferred-frame coupling (lensing correction), ensuring \alpha_{PF} \to 0 in the Newtonian limit, while the kinetic normalization of u_mu remains finite and independent.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the MOND sector reproduces \nabla \cdot [\mu \nabla \Phi] = 4\pi G \rho. The stiff vector u_mu provides the necessary off-ray preferred-frame stress to satisfy the slip-lock theorem (DC-013), correcting the lensing potential \Psi to match \Phi. Because the kinetic term is not multiplied by e^-y, the theory avoids the P7 strong-coupling wall that killed the khronometric candidate.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is structurally distinct from DC-010 (khronometric) because it uses a degenerate stiff vector (u_mu) rather than a khronon field, avoiding the finite-alpha_inf kill. It is distinct from DC-002 (AeST) because the preferred-frame coupling is explicitly screened by e^-y, whereas AeST has a constant 1/K_B coupling. It is distinct from DC-012/DC-013 (frameless) because it explicitly includes a preferred-frame carrier. It is distinct from previous multi-sector proposals (like FM-000008) by enforcing strict kinetic orthogonality: the screening factor applies ONLY to the PPN coupling, not the kinetic term, directly addressing the P7 frontier problem.
